relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own cover (arXiv:math/0608414v1 [math.CA], exponential asymptotics, trans-series and generalised Borel summation for analytic nonlinear rank-one ODE systems, single author) and matches the seeded key up to the ref() entry's slightly different capitalisation/expansion of the title. Citation status is NOT 'cited': the ref() entry exists (references.ts:5092) but grep over content/ finds no `\cite{costin1995}`, no `[costin1995]` and no cites-array entry — a bib orphan. Its only appearance is docs/audits/2026-07-20-qlift-literature-check.md:113, which lists it among resurgence foundations. This matters because the corpus has live, load-bearing Borel-summability content that currently leans on a single 2024 source: QOU/Mathlib/BorelStateIntegralSummability.lean is conditional on fantini-wheeler2024 Thm 1.4, and QOU/Mathlib/QGevreyOrder.lean and QAlienBridgeEquation.lean work with q-Gevrey orders and alien derivatives. The foundational generalised-Borel-summation-of-transseries statement those files implicitly assume is this document's main theorem, and it is uncited. Supporting rather than core because the folio's problem is q-difference, not rank-one ODE — the transfer of the summability theorem across that gap is not automatic and I have not checked its hypotheses in the q-setting.

keyResults.statement: For analytic nonlinear systems of ODEs at a rank-one irregular singularity, under non-degeneracy and integrability conditions the formal exponential (trans-)series solutions are Borel summable in Ecalle's sense, and the resummed functions are exactly the solutions decaying in a specified sector; the correspondence's dependence on the ray gives the local Stokes phenomenon.
keyResults.useForFolio: It is the classical-side anchor for 'trans-series are Borel summable and the ray-dependence IS the Stokes phenomenon', which is the pattern the q-difference Stokes work assumes. Citing it would make the analogy's classical leg explicit rather than tacit.

proposedActions.rationale: The Borel-summability/Stokes files carry no classical-ODE anchor; this reference already exists in references.ts and is exactly that anchor. Cite it as the classical leg, explicitly marked as the analogy's source and NOT as a transfer of the theorem to the q-difference setting.
